newsitem.title: USA: CFTC reviews soybean imports, US price drop-Letter.
newsitem.headline: CFTC reviews soybean imports, US price drop-Letter.

text.p: U.S. regulators started a review last month into a sharp drop in soybean prices that followed reports that South American soybeans would be imported for U.S. processing, a farm group announced Tuesday.

National Farmers Union announced the action by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission during a Senate hearing. It also released a letter from Brooksley Born, who chairs the CFTC, explaining the decision.

NFU president Leland Swenson said the 1996 "Freedom to Farm" law left farmers more vulnerable to price swings. He told the Agriculture Committee hearing that NFU wondered "could a major market trader manipulate the market by publicizing actions such as a major buy of import stocks?"

In a letter to the NFU dated July 25, Born said CFTC staff had been "closely monitoring trading in Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures for some time" because of tight supplies and "extremely small" stocks at delivery points for futures contracts.

"News reports about imports of South American soybeans for U.S. processing...were associated with a significant, negative impact on prices," Born wrote. "For that reason, our Chicago surveillance staff initiated a review of this matter.

"As part of this review, we ar examining the accuracy of the news reports. The (Commodity Exchange) Act specifically prohibits the dissemination of false and misleading market information. We also are examinilng certain cash and futures market activity to determine whether specific traders acted in any manner that might be in violation of the Commodity Exchange Act."
A CFTC spokesman was not immediately available to discuss the letter or possible conclusions from the review.
